summary: The ui component is the visual surface of the loop: TaskDisplay renders live task state (elapsed time, token counters, current tool), the TUI (ratatui app, palette, status_line, dashboard_widgets) owns the alternate-screen frame, and components.rs renders headers, step banners, tool-call rows, diffs, and checkpoints. On the loop it is a pure 'perceive' sink that projects AgentState, ToolCall progress, and Budget into human-readable frames — but on a touch canvas it doubles as the interface surface itself, where loop-stage nodes are drawn, dragged, and connected. It never mutates loop control; it observes and renders.
context_basis: Recommendations formed with ui read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), where the TUI owns rendering and stdout print functions become no-ops once set_tui_active(true).

examples.title: Mount TaskDisplay as the loop's live perceive frame
examples.intent: Give the operator a continuously updating projection of the running loop without touching control flow.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Reads AgentState, TokenUsage and current ToolCall on every tick and repaints; it adds zero iterations and consumes no budget, staying strictly downstream of the driver.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the TaskDisplay node opens a live HUD chip showing elapsed time, tokens in/out, and the current tool label.
touch_interaction.visual: Node pulses a soft cyan on each repaint tick; the fox glyph blinks when idle and wags its tail while a tool runs.

examples.mini_scenario: The driver enters Executing; TaskDisplay begins ticking, showing '3 tools, 12.4K tokens, 8s' as each shell_exec streams back.
examples.pitfall: Never let the display mutate the counters it reads — it is an observer; the atomics are owned by output/agent.

examples.title: Suppress stdout when the TUI owns the frame
examples.intent: Prevent raw prints from corrupting the ratatui alternate screen once the TUI launches.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: set_tui_active(true) turns every output print function into a no-op, so the loop's perceive channel funnels through one renderer instead of racing writers.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the TUI root node toggles the full-screen render surface, collapsing all inline print nodes into it.
touch_interaction.visual: The node expands to fill the canvas with a dimmed border; suppressed print nodes fade to 30% opacity.

examples.mini_scenario: Operator launches the TUI; thinking() and final_answer() calls silently drop because is_tui_active() is true, and the frame stays intact.
examples.pitfall: Forgetting set_tui_active(false) on exit leaves the loop mute — later CLI runs print nothing.

examples.title: Render a DiffView before an edit lands
examples.intent: Let the operator visually verify a file change on the canvas before it is committed to disk.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The diff renderer projects old vs new content as a red/green DiffView; the loop pauses at the verify node awaiting approval, gating the act transition.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading two fingers over the DiffView node expands the hunk list into a scrollable full-width panel of ± lines.
touch_interaction.visual: Added lines glow green, deleted lines red; an approve/reject badge pulses amber until the operator taps.

examples.mini_scenario: Agent proposes editing config.rs; the DiffView node shows +4/-2, operator spreads to inspect, taps approve, and the edit proceeds.
examples.pitfall: Do not render diffs while the TUI is active via stdout — display_file_diff returns early; route through the TUI widget instead.

examples.title: Drive multi-phase progress through ProgressPhase nodes
examples.intent: Give a spatial, staged read-out of a long multi-step plan.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: TaskProgress advances PhaseStatus (Pending→Active→Completed/Failed) as the driver crosses plan steps, mirroring the state machine without altering it.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging along the phase rail scrubs a preview cursor over each ProgressPhase, surfacing its status and percent.
touch_interaction.visual: Active phase fills a bright-cyan bar; completed phases show a green check, failed a red cross, with a live ETA chip.

examples.mini_scenario: A three-phase scaffold runs: 'plan' completes green, 'write' is active at 60%, 'verify' still pending — the rail reflects it live.
examples.pitfall: overall_progress divides by phase count — an empty phase list must return 0.0, never NaN into the bar width.

examples.title: Project the swarm as connected agent nodes
examples.intent: Show a parallel team of sub-agents as live nodes so the operator sees the fanout topology.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: swarm_viz reads each sub-agent's AgentState and renders them as siblings under the coordinator; it is a perceive-only mirror of the budget-scoped fanout.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching zooms the whole swarm out to a constellation of agent dots, or in to a single agent's tool timeline.
touch_interaction.visual: Each agent node glows by status — spinning for running, green settled for done — with edges to the coordinator pulsing on message flow.

examples.mini_scenario: The coordinator spawns four reviewers; the swarm view shows four cyan nodes, one turning red as its budget exhausts.
examples.pitfall: Rendering must tolerate agents appearing and vanishing mid-frame — never index a fixed-size slot array.

examples.title: Open the command palette as a searchable node index
examples.intent: Let the operator jump to any command/loop-node without leaving the canvas.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The palette lists PaletteEntry items backed by the command_registry; selecting one injects a control action into the driver.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing empty canvas raises a floating palette overlay filtered by fuzzy search as you type.
touch_interaction.visual: Overlay slides up with a frosted backdrop; the matched entry highlights and its category tag glows.

examples.mini_scenario: Operator long-presses, types 'undo', and taps the /undo entry — the loop rolls back the last edit via a checkpoint.
examples.pitfall: Palette entries must be sourced from is_known_command, not free text, or you dispatch an unregistered command.

examples.title: Render the header WorkshopContext as the loop identity chip
examples.intent: Anchor the canvas with the active model, endpoint, and execution mode.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: WorkshopContext is read-only config projected once; it frames the loop's identity but never gates iteration.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the header chip reveals the full endpoint URL and current ExecutionMode.
touch_interaction.visual: Chip tints by mode — grey normal, amber auto-edit, red yolo — so risk is visible at a glance.

examples.mini_scenario: Header shows 'Qwen3.5-122B · yolo' in red, warning the operator that confirmations are disabled.
examples.pitfall: The mode color is a safety signal — never render yolo in a calm color.

examples.title: Show a tool-call row per act step
examples.intent: Give one visible row per ToolCall as the loop acts.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: render_tool_call/success/error mirror each act transition; the row set is an append-only trace of the loop's actions.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking up scrolls the tool-call trace; flicking a row left reveals its raw args and result.
touch_interaction.visual: Running rows show a spinner, success rows a green tick, error rows a red cross with the error preview.

examples.mini_scenario: shell_exec row spins, then flips to a green tick 'exit 0'; the next file_edit row appears below it.
examples.pitfall: Error rows must carry the message — render_tool_error takes the error string; don't drop it.

examples.title: Make a Selection to scope a bulk operation
examples.intent: Let the operator multi-select nodes/files to batch a control action.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A Selection set becomes the scope for a subsequent act (e.g. approve all diffs), collapsing many decisions into one control transition.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press enters selection mode; subsequent taps toggle nodes into the Selection with a check overlay.
touch_interaction.visual: Selected nodes gain a bright ring and a running count badge; a floating action bar shows batch options.

examples.mini_scenario: Operator long-presses a diff, taps three more, and hits 'approve all' — four edits land in one control step.
examples.pitfall: A stale Selection after nodes change must be pruned, or a batch action targets vanished items.

examples.title: Pin a sticky status line for budget awareness
examples.intent: Keep budget and context usage in view regardless of scroll.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The sticky bar reads Budget/TokenUsage and context percent, projecting the loop's remaining runway without affecting it.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the sticky bar expands a breakdown of prompt vs completion tokens and context fill.
touch_interaction.visual: Bar fills green→amber→red as context approaches the window limit; pulses red near saturation.

examples.mini_scenario: At 82% context the sticky bar turns amber, cueing the operator to consider a summary before the next turn.
examples.pitfall: Context percent must clamp to [0,1] before mapping to bar color; an over-100% value is a bug upstream.

examples.title: Animate a spinner while the loop reasons
examples.intent: Signal that the loop is thinking, not hung.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The GardenSpinner ticks on a timer during the reason phase; purely cosmetic, it adds no budget and gates nothing.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the reasoning node pauses/resumes the spinner animation for a still snapshot.
touch_interaction.visual: A growing-plant glyph cycles frames; it finishes with a bloom on success or a wilt on failure.

examples.mini_scenario: While the model streams a plan, the spinner grows; when the plan arrives it blooms and hands off to act.
examples.pitfall: Spinner frames must be suppressed in plain/JSON mode — a spinning glyph corrupts piped output.

examples.title: Render a checkpoint-saved badge on the timeline
examples.intent: Mark durable rollback points the operator can return to.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: render_checkpoint_saved emits a marker when the session persists a Checkpoint, giving the loop visible undo anchors.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a checkpoint marker offers 'restore to here', wiring into /undo.
touch_interaction.visual: A small anchor badge with the task id; glows green on save, blue when it is the active restore target.

examples.mini_scenario: After a successful edit batch, a checkpoint marker appears; later the operator double-taps it to revert.
examples.pitfall: The marker's task_id must match the real checkpoint or /timeline restores the wrong state.

examples.title: Two-finger pan the loop canvas
examples.intent: Move around a large graph of loop-stage nodes.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Pure viewport control over the perceive surface; it repositions the camera, never the loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Two-finger drag pans the canvas; adding rotation reorients the graph layout around the pivot.
touch_interaction.visual: Nodes glide with momentum; off-screen active nodes leave a comet trail toward their direction.

examples.mini_scenario: Operator two-finger pans from the coordinator toward a busy sub-agent cluster to watch its tool trace.
examples.pitfall: Panning must not deselect the active Selection — treat camera moves as orthogonal to selection state.

examples.title: Draw an edge to wire a downstream node
examples.intent: Let the operator connect one loop node's output to another's input on the canvas.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Drawing a connection declares a wiring edge that the driver later honors, shaping which component feeds which on the loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging from a node's output port to another's input port draws a live edge that snaps when released.
touch_interaction.visual: The edge renders as a bright bezier that pulses in the direction of intended data flow once connected.

examples.mini_scenario: Operator draws an edge from the diff-viewer node to the checkpoint node so every approved diff auto-checkpoints.
examples.pitfall: Reject edges that create a cycle in the perceive→act graph, or the loop projection deadlocks.

examples.title: Flash a warning banner on a recoverable error
examples.intent: Make a soft failure visible without halting the loop.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: render_warning projects a recoverable condition during verify; the loop may still transition to ErrorRecovery, the banner just informs.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the warning banner expands the classified failure detail and suggested recovery.
touch_interaction.visual: Amber banner slides in and auto-dismisses; the offending node briefly outlines amber.

examples.mini_scenario: A test flakes; a warning banner notes 'retry 1/3' while the loop re-enters the act step.
examples.pitfall: Warnings must not look like hard errors — reserve red for terminal failure, amber for recoverable.

examples.title: Render the final answer as a settled node
examples.intent: Present the loop's conclusion clearly at Completed.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: render_assistant_response draws the final content; in streaming mode it is skipped to avoid duplicating live-streamed tokens.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading over the answer node expands markdown rendering with code blocks and links.
touch_interaction.visual: Node settles to a calm green border on Completed; a subtle checkmark seals it.

examples.mini_scenario: Loop reaches Completed; the answer node renders the summary with a green seal and stops ticking.
examples.pitfall: In streaming mode do not re-render the answer — is_streaming_mode() must gate it or it prints twice.

examples.title: Zoom a single tool node to full telemetry
examples.intent: Inspect one ToolCall's args, output, and timing without leaving context.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Read-only detail expansion; drills into a captured ToolCall record, altering nothing on the loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch-in on a tool row scales it from a one-line chip to a full telemetry card.
touch_interaction.visual: Card grows to show duration, exit code, and a scrollable result; edges to neighbors dim to focus it.

examples.mini_scenario: Operator pinches a shell_exec row to read the full 200-line stdout that the summary truncated.
examples.pitfall: The card must page long output — never render an unbounded result string into the frame.

examples.title: Render a step banner at each plan transition
examples.intent: Announce each numbered step as the driver advances the plan.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: step_start emits a banner on each step boundary, mirroring the Planning→Executing transitions in the state machine.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking horizontally across step banners scrubs the plan timeline forward/back for review.
touch_interaction.visual: Each banner slides in with the step number badge; the active step's badge glows brighter.

examples.mini_scenario: 'Step 3: run tests' banner appears as the driver crosses into the third plan step.
examples.pitfall: Step banners are suppressed in compact/quiet/JSON — don't rely on them for machine parsing.

examples.title: Collapse the dashboard to a summary chip
examples.intent: Reduce a busy dashboard to a glanceable chip when the operator zooms out.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: dashboard_widgets aggregate multiple loop reads (tokens, tools, phases) into one collapsible view; observation only.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch-out collapses the dashboard grid into a single summary chip with an overall health dot.
touch_interaction.visual: Widgets fold into a chip; the health dot is green while all phases progress, amber if any stalls.

examples.mini_scenario: Operator zooms out to a chip during a long run, expanding it only when the health dot turns amber.
examples.pitfall: The collapsed chip must still reflect failures — don't hide a failed phase behind a green dot.

examples.title: Hand rendering back to CLI on TUI exit
examples.intent: Cleanly return the perceive channel to inline printing when leaving the TUI.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: set_tui_active(false) re-enables output print functions so subsequent loop turns render inline; a lifecycle boundary, not a control change.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the TUI root node again dismisses the full-screen surface and restores inline node prints.
touch_interaction.visual: The full-screen frame contracts back into the canvas; faded inline print nodes return to full opacity.

examples.mini_scenario: Operator exits the TUI; is_tui_active() flips false and the next final_answer prints inline as expected.
examples.pitfall: Restore the alternate screen and the active flag together — leaving the flag set silences all later output.
